s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal distinction between direct and indirect taxes in India?
o: In a direct tax, impact and incidence fall on the same person, whereas the burden of an indirect tax can be shifted to the consumer
In a direct tax, the burden is shifted through prices, whereas an indirect tax cannot be shifted
Direct taxes are collected by intermediaries, whereas indirect taxes are collected by the income-tax authorities
Both direct and indirect taxes are collected only from the final consumer
x: The impact and incidence of a direct tax fall on the same person and cannot ordinarily be shifted. An indirect tax is collected through an intermediary and passed on to the consumer through the price.
tq: Split the options by checking whether the tax burden can be shifted.
sec: Direct vs indirect taxes - classification and base  [APPSC]

Direct taxes — Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
Indirect taxes — Central Board of Direct Taxes

x: Direct taxes are administered by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), while indirect taxes are administered by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC).
tq: Use the authority-swap trap by matching each tax category with its administering body.
sec: Direct vs indirect taxes - classification and base  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes a tax?
o: A temporary levy retained only until a specified purpose is achieved
A compulsory contribution imposed under legal authority without a direct quid pro quo
A voluntary payment made for a specific government service
An additional percentage charge imposed only on an existing tax
x: A tax is a compulsory pecuniary contribution imposed under the authority of law to finance government, without a direct quid pro quo.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Fee — payment for a specific service involving quid pro quo
Cess — additional charge on tax payable, usually permanent
Surcharge — tax on tax for a specific purpose that ends when the purpose is met
Tax — payment made only when a specific service is received
x: A fee is paid for a specific service and involves quid pro quo. A cess is a tax on tax for a specific purpose, while a surcharge is an additional charge on tax payable.
tq: Use the exact meaning of each closely related levy to eliminate swapped definitions.
